title: Pano AI cameras on Xcel and CORE Electric towers spot the Bear Creek Fire; helicopters hold it to three acres
summary: Utility-funded Pano AI cameras detected smoke from the 16 June 2024 Bear Creek Fire in Douglas County, Colorado; helicopters were dispatched within 30 minutes and the fire was held to three acres.
account: On 16 June 2024 Pano AI wildfire-detection cameras on Xcel Energy and CORE Electric Cooperative towers detected smoke. It came from a lightning-caused fire in Douglas County, Colorado. According to Renewable Energy World (18 July 2024), emergency services dispatched two helicopters within 30 minutes of the identification, when the fire was 0.25 acres. The helicopters dropped 17,765 gallons of water over six hours and the fire was limited to three acres. Denver7 (17 July 2024) reported that the fire was contained within a day and was first spotted by the AI-equipped cameras. CORE's wildfire mitigation manager Jordan Ambrogi said alerts typically arrive 10 to 12 minutes after smoke is detected. The utilities, however, said the cameras identified the fire “simultaneously” with the U.S. Forest Service. So the cameras' independent contribution to containment rests on the operators' own statements (CORE interim CEO Pam Feuerstein). The OECD AI Incidents Monitor carries a separate positively framed record of Xcel's November 2023 Pano AI deployment.
purpose: Pano AI cameras rotate 360 degrees on mountaintop towers and use AI to detect smoke plumes. They alert utilities and fire agencies with a triangulated location. Detecting this fire early was the intended use.
system: Pano AI wildfire detection cameras (Pano Rapid Detect)
deployer: Xcel Energy and CORE Electric Cooperative
taxonomy_note: Fire spread averted is read as reduced potential for harm; Trustible's description stresses legal harm.

ratings.reason: The fire was held to three acres after helicopters were dispatched within 30 minutes. CORE's CEO called the detection and location “crucial”. Simultaneous Forest Service identification limits what can be attributed to the cameras.
CORE Electric and Xcel Energy obtained a fast, located alert supporting their wildfire mitigation strategy. Denver7 quotes CORE's Jordan Ambrogi saying alerts typically beat 911 calls.
No individual beneficiary is documented in the sources.

ai_role.statement: The AI smoke detection produced the alert and location that the utilities and Denver7 describe. The sources are independent news reports quoting operator staff, not an official filing. The operators themselves say the Forest Service identified the fire simultaneously. So the counterfactual contribution of the AI to the three-acre outcome is unverified.
